This question is about gradient, intercepts and equations of straight lines; parallel and perpendicular lines. Answers should be exact or correct to 3 significant figures.

(a) Find the equation of the line through (−1, −4) and (−3, −6) in the form y = mx + c. [4]

(b) A student claims: "The gradient of the line through (2, 5) and (6, 3) is (6 − 2)/(3 − 5) = −2." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [3]
items.answer: (a) y = x − 3 (b) Gradient is change in y over change in x: (3 − 5)/(6 − 2) = −1/2.
items.markingKey: (a) [4 marks] m = 1 (A1); substitute a point (M1); y = x − 3 (A1). (b) [3 marks] Gradient is change in y over change in x: (3 − 5)/(6 − 2) = −1/2. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

This question is about sum of infinite geometric sequences. Answers should be exact or correct to 3 significant figures.

(a) "Because the series 1 + 0.9 + 0.81 + … has infinitely many terms, its sum must be infinite." Explain the flaw in this statement. [2]

(b) A patient takes 200 mg of a medicine every 12 hours. Just before each new dose 20% of the previous amount remains in the body. Find the long-term amount in the body immediately after a dose. [4]

(c) The sum to infinity of a geometric series is 120 and its first term is 30. (i) Find the common ratio. (ii) Find the least number of terms for which Sₙ is within 2% of S∞. (iii) Explain why a sum to infinity exists for this series. [7]
items.answer: (a) Infinitely many terms can have a finite sum when they shrink fast enough: r = 0.9 gives S∞ = 1/(1 − 0.9) = 10. (b) 250 mg (c) (i) r = 0.75 (ii) n = 14 (iii) |r| < 1
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] Infinitely many terms can have a finite sum when they shrink fast enough: r = 0.9 gives S∞ = 1/(1 − 0.9) = 10. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (b) [4 marks] Amount after nth dose = 200(1 + 0.2 + 0.2² + … ) (M1); S∞ = 200/(1 − 0.2) (M1) = 250 mg (A1). (c) [7 marks] (i) 30/(1 − r) = 120 (M1) → r = 0.75 (A1). (ii) S∞ − Sₙ < 0.02 × 120, i.e. 120 × 0.75ⁿ < 2.40 (M1) (GDC or logs) n = 14 (A1 A1). (iii) R1 |0.75| < 1 so rⁿ → 0.

This question is about combined events, mutually exclusive and independent events; conditional probability. Answers should be exact or correct to 3 significant figures.

(a) P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.7 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.45. Determine, with a reason, whether A and B are (i) mutually exclusive; (ii) independent. [3]

(b) The probability that a seed is treated is 0.8. If a seed is treated, the probability that the seed germinates is 0.6; otherwise it is 0.4. Find the probability that the seed germinates. [3]

(c) A screening test for a genetic condition affects 1% of a population. The test is positive for 99% of people with the condition and negative for 90% of people without it. (i) Draw a tree diagram. (ii) Find the probability that a randomly chosen person tests positive. (iii) Find the probability that a person who tests positive has the condition. (iv) Comment on your answer to (iii) in context. [7]
items.markingKey: (a) [3 marks] (i) R1 P(A ∩ B) = 0.45 ≠ 0, so not mutually exclusive. (ii) P(A)P(B) = 0.42 (M1); R1 not equal to P(A ∩ B), so not independent. (b) [3 marks] Tree diagram (M1); 0.8 × 0.6 + 0.2 × 0.4 (M1) = 14/25 (0.560) (A1). (c) [7 marks] (i) A2. (ii) 0.01 × 0.99 + 0.99 × 0.1 (M1) = 0.109 (A1). (iii) 0.00990/0.109 (M1) = 0.0909 (A1). (iv) R1 most positive results are false positives because the condition is rare – a second test is needed.

This question is about logarithmic, logistic and piecewise models. Answers should be exact or correct to 3 significant figures.

(a) A student claims: "A logistic population eventually exceeds its carrying capacity because it never stops growing." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [2]

(b) The height h cm of a sapling x weeks after planting is modelled by h(x) = 5.5 + 10.9 ln x, x ≥ 1. Find h(54) and the time when h = 54.8 cm. [3]

(c) The number of fish in a lake t years after observations began is modelled by N(t) = 5000/(1 + 14.7e^(−0.61t)). (i) Find the initial number and the carrying capacity. (iv) Compare the logistic model with an exponential model N = 318e^(0.61t) for large t. [8]
items.answer: (a) The population approaches L asymptotically from below; 1 + Ce^(−kt) > 1 so P < L for all t. (b) h(54) = 49.0 cm; x = 92.1 weeks (c) (i) 318, 5000 (ii) 8.01 (iii) 4.41 (iv) the exponential grows without bound
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] The population approaches L asymptotically from below; 1 + Ce^(−kt) > 1 so P < L for all t. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (b) [3 marks] h(54) = 49.0 (A1); ln x = (54.8 − 5.5)/10.9 (M1); x = 92.1 (A1). (c) [8 marks] (i) A1 A1. (ii) M1 A1 8.01. (iii) 1 + 14.7e^(−0.61t) = 2 (M1) ⇒ t = ln(14.7)/0.61 = 4.41 (A1). (iv) R1 similar for small t; R1 the exponential model exceeds the carrying capacity, the logistic levels off.
